description: We are students aspiring to contribute to NASA's space exploration goals in any way we can.
summary: FireCast is a responsive web application aimed for use by live responders. It queries live information from MODIS satellites and presents the data in a friendly, meaningful way. The project allows live responders to view local anomalies and past fire events in a beautifully presented way, which can enable them to better plan and coordinate rescue operations, potentially saving lives and properties which would otherwise be lost.
details:
This project is a web application that fetches data from NASA's satellite sensor datasets. From the Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC API, data is processed and displayed in a creative 3D globe format with multiple toggleable layers. Information is displayed on side about major fires and their related content. On the globe, hotspots are highlighted and dynamic for quick comprehension. In addition to live data, documented historical records could be accessed from the website. There is also a calendar feature that allows the user to see fire-data from a specific location.

The benefit of using this interface is that it provides an easy visualization of historic fires around the world, current fires happening now, and where they are predicted to spread. First responders and emergency handlers can utilize this website to analyze regions for accurate fire predictions, which is especially important in fire disasters, where every second can prevent the spread of fire and save lives.

The project relies on Microsoft's Planetary Computer API, which has been proven to be an immensely valuable asset to our data gathering workflow. The front end relies on a python Flask server. Artificial Intelligence tools were minimally used throughout the entirety of this project's development. Claude was used to optimize our frontend and organize the data collected, while the majority of the code logic, structure, and implementation were done by us humans.
